column2: changing how often bonus food appears changes a strategy without touching any food type,Because Java interfaces cannot construct objects,Because the strategy must be an interface and the creator must be a class,,2,Two independent axes of variation. Combining them would mean every new food type had to be added to every existing spawn rule.,2

callers must simply be careful,,2,"The demo builds a new strategy per game, so the bug never appears - which is exactly what makes it dangerous. A convention that only works while everyone remembers it is not a safeguard.",2

nothing else depends on it,"It enforces that food never appears under the snake - and the collision check depends on it, because 'newHead equals the tail' and 'newHead equals the food' can then never both be true at once",It enforces that food is never adjacent to the head,"It enforces the board size limit, which Board depends on",,2,This is why the collision condition could be simplified to drop its eatsFood term. The simplification is only valid while this loop holds - an invariant in one method quietly propping up a line in another.,2

the strategy makes every decision,"One FoodItem. The strategy decides WHICH creator, the creator decides WHICH FoodItem subclass to construct, and SnakeGame had already decided WHERE - three separate decisions made by three different objects",Three objects - one per layer,Two objects - a creator and an item - because the creator is built fresh each time,,2,"The creators are pre-built and reused inside each strategy, so only the FoodItem is new. Tracing which object makes which decision is the clearest way to see why the layers exist.",2

the real bug was elsewhere,"A FoodItem holds a position, so two foods must be different objects. A parking spot holds occupancy, so sharing one made every compact spot the same spot. Both are stateful, which is exactly why neither should be cached",Because food is created more often than spots,Because FoodCreator is abstract and SpotFactory is concrete,,2,"Same rule reached from the snake side: cache stateless objects freely, never cache stateful ones. The creators themselves ARE cached inside each strategy, and that is fine because they hold nothing.",2
